name: IKI Small Grants

funder.name: German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN)

summary: Grants from Germany's International Climate Initiative for small local organisations in ODA-eligible countries running single-country climate and biodiversity projects; the current call focuses on nature-based solutions and pairs funding with capacity development.

steps: Submit organisation information and documents for eligibility check
Full proposal and budget, by invitation
Review and discussion with GIZ, if selected

eligibility.rule: Nonprofit or company pursuing nonprofit project goals, with no individual, one-person or government applicants.
Financially and legally independent, with no parent organisation based in a non-ODA country if a branch
Operating for at least 3 years by the submission deadline
Average yearly revenue of €60,000 to €500,000 over the last 3 years
Have dedicated accounting staff, internal and external controls, and accounting software meeting national standards.
Request no more than your average annual revenue over the past three years.
The project is in one country, at local, sub-national or national level
Project lasts 12–24 months, or up to 36 months in justified exceptional cases

documents: Dated, signed accounts for the last 3 available years, the latest period ending June 2025 or later.
Accounting guidelines, with separate procurement standards if these are not already covered.
Full, signed external audit reports, if your financial statements are externally audited.
English translations of official organisation documents and register entries, where needed.

applicant_types.quote: Applicants should be not-for-profit organisations and private companies if they pursue non-profit objectives as part of their proposed project.

geography.quote: Projects must be implemented in countries that fulfil the criteria for Official Development Assistance (ODA) with the same exemptions for applying organisations mentioned under 2.1.

access.quote: The international call for proposals addresses local organisations based in ODA-eligible countries with an average annual revenue of between EUR 60,000 and EUR 500,000.

window.quote: The 8th IKI Small Grants 'Call for Proposals' will open on 15 November 2026 and the application period will be closed on 8 January 2027.

amount.quote: IKI Small Grants provides funding between EUR 60,000 and EUR 200,000.

consortium_required.quote: Consortia are not eligible and forwarding funds to other implementing organisations is not permitted.

effort.quote: must first pass an eligibility check. In this first stage, applicants are asked to provide information on their organisations and submit the following supporting documents:
Interested organisations must submit this information and these documents via the application platform by January 08, 2027.
Qualified organisations will subsequently be invited to submit their project proposals and budget until March 16, 2027, through the same platform.
The submitted proposals then undergo a selection process, and applicant organisations will be informed in due time.
Please note that a review phase, including close exchange between the applicant organisation and GIZ, will follow the final selection for funding.

eligibility.quote: Applicants should be not-for-profit organisations and private companies if they pursue non-profit objectives as part of their proposed project. No individuals, natural persons, one-person organisations or governmental organisations are eligible

Applicants must be based and registered in countries that meet the criteria for Official Development Assistance (ODA) as defined by the Development Assistance Committee (DAC) of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)1. Organisations must be financially and legally independent and branches of organisations based in a non-eligible country cannot be funded.
The applicant organisation must have been operative for at least three years (36 months by the time of the submission deadline).
Over the last three years the applicant organisation must have generated an average annual revenue of at least EUR 60,000 and no more than EUR 500,000.

The applicant organisation must have dedicated accounting staff and have accounting principles that ensure internal as well as external control mechanisms. It must also employ a software-based accounting system that complies with respective national standards.
Furthermore, the requested funding volume must not exceed the average annual revenue of the implementing organisation over the past three years.
Projects must be implemented on a local, sub-national or national level. No multi-country projects can be funded.
Projects must have a duration of at least twelve months and no more than two years. In exceptional cases, durations of up to three years can be acceptable if justified appropriately.

after_award.quote: Successful implementation in the IKI Small Grants programme includes participation in capacity development curriculum.

documents.quote: Registration certificates Financial statements covering the last three available years, including relevant information on the applicant's revenue Note: The most recent financial statements must cover a period ending no earlier than June 2025.
Completed revenue template Accounting & procurement guidelines
These statements must be dated and signed and should be scanned documents.
Internal procurement standards need to be submitted by the applicant if they are not covered as part of the internal accounting guidelines.
If your financial statements are subject to external audits, then these must be submitted in full. External financial audits must be signed by the auditor and contain his or her findings.

Official documents of the organisation (e.g. accounting guidelines) and register entries must be submitted with additional English translations. While these translations are required, they need not be notarised.
